hasStrongType_maximalFunction.statement: If $0 < p_1 < p_2$, then the maximal function $\mathrm{maximalFunction}(\mu, \mathcal{B}, c, r, p_1)$ has strong type $(p_2, p_2)$ with respect to $\mu$ and $\mu$, with constant $C_{2.0.6}(A, p_1, p_2)$.
hasStrongType_maximalFunction.sketch: It is deduced from the case of exponent $1$, `hasStrongType_maximalFunction_one` (strong type $(p,p)$ for $p > 1$), using the relation $p_1 < p_2$ between the exponents.

hasStrongType_maximalFunction_one.statement: If $p > 1$, then the maximal function $\mathrm{maximalFunction}(\mu, \mathcal{B}, c, r, 1)$ has strong type $(p, p)$ with respect to $\mu$ and $\mu$, with constant $C_{MB}(A, p)$ (a special case of (2.0.44)).
hasStrongType_maximalFunction_one.sketch: Apply the Marcinkiewicz real interpolation theorem `exists_hasStrongType_real_interpolation` to the (sublinear) maximal operator, interpolating between two weak-type estimates.
